title: Early-warning outlier predictor and routed alerting playbook for usage/cost/latency
creator: Mariana Ortiz
description: Build a phased system that uses short-term forecasting + statistical outlier signals to surface early-warning alerts on usage, cost, and tail latency for customers and infra. Unlike the current discrete spike detectors, this work combines: 1) a lightweight autoregressive forecaster that predicts 5–60m expected telemetry windows, 2) a residual-based outlier scorer that contextualizes changes by customer cohort (plan/region/model), and 3) an alert-routing layer that maps severity to channels (console, Slack, PagerDuty, email) and to investigation playbooks. Goals: detect degradations earlier with fewer false positives, surface suggested mitigations (e.g., autoscaling trigger, model fallback), and provide feedback for model retraining from labeled incidents.
acceptance_criteria: Predictive detector emits anomaly candidate at least 10 minutes before peak in 70% of test incidents (historical backtest)
False positive rate under 5% when evaluated across high-volume customers during a 30-day validation window
Alerts include severity, top-3 contributing signals (usage, median latency, error-rate), cohort attribution, and a recommended playbook link
Routing policy sends P0 to on-call via PagerDuty and P1 to team Slack channel; console shows suppressible alert with one-click acknowledge
All alert metadata stored in telemetry index with TTL aligned to privacy policy and available for postmortem queries
implementation_notes: Signal inputs: per-customer per-route token consumption, 95th/99th latency, model selection rate, error counts, and billing delta over 1h/24h baselines
Model: lightweight Holt-Winters / simple AR(1) with seasonal de-trending for cost/usage; exponentially-weighted residual z-score as outlier signal to keep runtime <200ms per customer-bucket
Enrichment: join with customer tier, dedicated vs hosted, region, recent rollout flags, and active rollouts from console API
Detector windowing: rolling 5m/15m/60m horizons with cascading alert thresholds to reduce flapping
Backfill safety: ensure detector ignores historical backlog-induced spikes by marking ingestion lag and applying corrective normalization
Storage: write candidates to telemetry-alerts topic (Kafka) and index to ClickHouse for fast analytics; follow retention policy: 90d detailed, 365d aggregated
Routing: policy service maps to escalation path; include cost-sensitivity multiplier so high-billing customers increase urgency
Grace periods: configurable per-customer silence windows and maintenance windows stored on customer profile
Observability: add metric for lead-time-to-detection, precision@k, and average alert noise per customer-tier
Privacy: strip PII from alert payloads; include customer ID references only as hashed tokens for Slack notifications
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: forecast models may be brittle during product launches — Mitigation: require rollout flag logic to disable predictive alerts during active canary windows
Risk: noisy low-volume customers generating false positives — Mitigation: cohort-aware minimum volume gating and adaptive thresholds
Risk: alert storming during infra incidents — Mitigation: cross-signal suppression and global incident mode that suppresses non-actionable alerts
Risk: billing/privacy concerns for aggregated alerts — Mitigation: consult legal and redact granular usage; provide opt-out for usage sharing in alerts
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (lab): train and backtest models on 12 months of telemetry; validate on recent 90d; produce evaluation report
Phase 1 (pilot): enable predictive alerts for internal Redwood services + 5 opt-in customers; collect feedback for 2 weeks
Phase 2 (slow rollout): enable for 10% of eligible customers with exponential ramp; monitor false positive rate and lead-time metrics
Phase 3 (GA): enable by default with opt-out; publish runbook and customer-facing docs
runbook_snippet: When alert severity == P0: immediately page on-call. Run initial triage: check global incident flag (console/infra); query last 60m: sum(token_count), p95 latency, model-change events. If model-change or rollout=true, mark as rollout-induced and follow rollout rollback playbook.

When alert severity == P1: post to team Slack alert channel with link to ticket template and suggested investigation checklist. If billing spike and no model changes, trigger cost-protection guardrail suggestion (reduce batch size, pin to cheaper quantized variant).

Investigation queries: SELECT customer_hash, route, SUM(tokens) as tokens_60m, PERCENTILE_CONT(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (latency) as p95_lat FROM telemetry WHERE ts > now() - interval '60 minutes' GROUP BY customer_hash, route ORDER BY tokens_60m DESC LIMIT 20; (Example provided for ClickHouse)
